attempts: Attempt 1: Create a scenario where a task's ChangeSet touches a sibling task's owned_surfaces. Expectation: boundaryCheck is called on the settled ChangeSet after empty-diff resolution (AC-4) and the task escalates with passed:false instead of entering the verify-loop panel. Actual behavior: No boundaryCheck call exists anywhere in the workflow; the violation passes through unflagged and the task proceeds to the panel normally, failing to end early as the spec requires. Test 13 explicitly fails with 'a boundary violation must return the task as passed:false, never reaching the panel'.

Attempt 2: Construct a lens verdict with multiple findings, one citing only a sibling-owned criterion. Expectation: stripForeignFindings removes that finding before adjudicate (AC-11), preventing it from reaching the fixer, never entering ctx.seen, and the task can pass if remaining findings are fixed. Actual behavior: No stripForeignFindings call site exists in the workflow at any point; the foreign finding reaches the adjudicator, the fixer, and the dedupe list unchanged, wasting budget on a finding no fixer in this task can resolve. Test 17 explicitly fails with 'stripForeignFindings must run on the round's verdicts before they reach adjudicate'.

Attempt 3: A code Fixer returns a ChangeSet with notes='TEST-ONLY: the test asserts X but spec says Y' for a finding routed by location to the code path. Expectation: fixOutcome recognizes TEST-ONLY: prefix (distinct from DISPUTE), the finding is re-routed to the Test Author repair path once in the same round, never to the dispute judge, and never counted in applied fixes (AC-16). Actual behavior: No fixOutcome function exists to classify the notes; no TEST-ONLY re-routing branch exists; the finding is treated as a normal DISPUTE or applied fix, wasting a fixer attempt on a defect that belongs in a test the fixer cannot edit. Tests 11, 19, and 20 all fail on this path.
